parts:
Yes. In Tennessee there *are* financial relief options for domestic violence survivors, but unfortunately they are scattered across different programs and can be overwhelming to navigate alone. Based on what you described, you may qualify for several types of assistance at the same time, especially because your injury affected your ability to work and you’re losing alimony income.

The biggest one you should look into immediately is Tennessee’s Criminal Injuries Compensation Program. It can sometimes help cover:
- Lost wages/income
- Medical bills
- Counseling
- Loss of financial support
- Other crime-related expenses

And importantly, domestic violence victims can qualify. citeturn0search6turn0search5

You already took a major step by making the police report. That matters because many victim compensation programs require documentation of the crime. Since you also have surgery, ongoing treatment, MRIs, therapy, and documented loss of work ability, your case is stronger than someone with no paper trail.

You should also immediately contact:
- urlTennessee Coalition to End Domestic & Sexual Violencehttps://tncoalition.org/
- Tennessee statewide DV hotline: 1-800-356-6767 citeturn0search4

Do not think of the hotline as “just crisis shelter.” They often connect survivors to:
- Emergency grants
- Utility assistance
- Rent help
- Relocation help
- Legal advocates
- Counseling funding
- Crime victim compensation advocates who help fill out the paperwork

There are also housing and emergency assistance programs in Tennessee that can help with rent, utilities, deposits, and short-term stabilization if you are at risk financially because of the abuse situation. citeturn0search15turn0search12

You may additionally qualify for:
- SNAP/food assistance citeturn0search1
- Temporary Families First/TANF cash assistance
- Medicaid/TennCare based on reduced income
- Workforce retraining or vocational rehab if your injury limits your previous work
- Social Security Disability or short-term disability if your surgeon documents inability to perform your occupation

Since your business income is unstable right now and you may not physically be able to return to office work, I would strongly encourage you to frame this as:
> “Crime-related injury causing loss of earning capacity and financial instability.”

That language matters.

You also likely need a victim advocate or legal aid attorney helping you package everything together instead of trying to apply one-by-one alone.

For Tennessee legal help specifically:
- urlLegal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee & the Cumberlandshttps://las.org/
- urlWest Tennessee Legal Serviceshttps://wtls.org/
- urlLegal Aid of East Tennesseehttps://www.laet.org/ citeturn0search14

They can sometimes help with:
- Extending or modifying support arrangements
- Protection orders
- Compensation applications
- Housing rights
- Employment protections
- Divorce/alimony enforcement issues
- Civil claims related to abuse

One important thing:
Do not wait until alimony ends or bills pile up further before applying. Many of these programs move slowly and some only help prospectively, not retroactively.

I would prioritize these 3 things this week:
1. Apply for Tennessee Criminal Injuries Compensation
2. Call the Tennessee DV coalition and ask for a victim advocate assigned to you
3. Meet with legal aid specifically about financial stability and loss of income after abuse-related injury

You have more documentation than many survivors do:
- Police report
- Medical timeline
- Surgery
- Therapy
- Lost work ability
- Witness trauma involving your son
- Ongoing treatment

That combination matters.
